_meta.project: Maryland Open Platform (MOP) — UMD Smith School
_meta.note: This file is the primary knowledge source for the NL-to-SQL agent. Keep it current as datasets are updated.

state_name_casing.problem: State names are stored in different cases across tables. JOINs will silently fail without normalization.
state_name_casing.sql_fix: Always wrap state in LOWER() before joining: LOWER(a.state) = LOWER(b.state)
state_name_casing.example: SELECT a.state, a.financial_literacy, b.Contracts FROM finra_state a JOIN contract_state b ON LOWER(a.state) = LOWER(b.state) WHERE a.Year = 2021 AND b.year = '2024'

special_character_columns.problem: These column names contain commas and ampersands and MUST be double-quoted in all SQL

columns_with_spaces.problem: Several columns in contract and spending tables contain spaces and must be quoted

year_as_string_in_contract_tables.problem: The period column in contract and spending tables is a STRING, not an integer. Values are '2024' or '2020-2024'. The latter is a precomputed multi-year summary whose exact aggregation method is not documented in this repository; do not describe it as a five-year sum or add it to the 2024 row.
year_as_string_in_contract_tables.sql_fix: Filter with: WHERE year = '2024'  (not WHERE year = 2024)

gov_year_label.note: The Year column in gov_state, gov_county, gov_congress contains string value 'Fiscal Year 2023', not an integer. The data is single-year (FY2023 only).
gov_year_label.sql_fix: Do not filter by year for gov tables — there is only one year of data.

finra_years_available.note: finra_state has data for survey years 2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021. finra_county and finra_congress only have 2021.

state_flow_duplicate_columns.problem: In state_flow, rcpt_st_cd and rcpt_state_name contain identical data (both are full state names). Likewise subawardee_st_cd = subawardee_state_name. Always use the *_state_name versions for clarity.
state_flow_duplicate_columns.fix: Use rcpt_state_name and subawardee_state_name in all queries on state_flow

congress_flow_integer_district_id.problem: congress_flow.prime_awardee_stcd118 and subawardee_stcd118 are INTEGER codes, not the 'MD-08' string format used in other congress-level tables. A direct equality to cd_118 is wrong.
congress_flow_integer_district_id.fix: For filtering, use rcpt_cd_name/subawardee_cd_name. contract_congress carries state_fips and can be canonicalized directly. ACS/FINRA/government congressional tables lack state_fips, so first join their cd_118 to a DISTINCT contract_congress cd_118/state_fips mapping, then use CAST(CONCAT(CAST(state_fips AS INTEGER), RIGHT(cd_118, 2)) AS INTEGER) to join prime_awardee_stcd118 (outflow) or subawardee_stcd118 (inflow).

county_flow_fips_as_integer.note: county_flow.rcpt_cty and subawardee_cty are integer FIPS codes — safe to join directly with gov_county.fips and acs_county.fips

contract_county_agency_state_aggregate_r.problem: contract_county_agency has rows where county_fips = 1 (or single-digit values) — these are state-level aggregate rows, not real counties.
contract_county_agency_state_aggregate_r.fix: Always add WHERE county_fips > 1000 when querying contract_county_agency for county-level results

state_identifier.description: Full U.S. state name. Case varies by table — always use LOWER() when joining. See _critical_warnings.state_name_casing.

county_identifier.description: County name without 'County' suffix. Lowercase in most tables, UPPERCASE in contract tables.
county_identifier.join_key: fips is the reliable join key between county-level tables — prefer fips over county name string matching

fips_identifier.description: Federal Information Processing Standards code — unique 4-5 digit integer identifying each US county. Reliable cross-table join key.

congressional_district_identifier.description: 118th Congressional District code in format STATE_ABBR-DISTRICT_NUMBER. e.g. 'MD-08', 'CA-12', 'AK-00' (at-large). Fixed column name across all congress-level tables.

acs_state.description: Curated American Community Survey (ACS) demographic data aggregated at the U.S. state level. This runtime table is a subset of the broader upstream ACS documentation and includes only the variables listed below.
acs_state.grain: One row per state per year
critical_notes: Runtime coverage is narrower than the upstream ACS source documentation: this table has only Age 18-65, not detailed age bands such as 85+; it has no sex/gender columns and no associate-degree or less-than-9th-grade column.

Race/ethnicity, age, education, income, poverty, and housing fields are separate marginal percentages, not a joint cross-tabulation. They cannot answer intersections such as Hispanic adults with bachelor's degrees or women with graduate degrees.

Education percentages describe adults age 25+, but this table does not contain the number of adults age 25+. Report the percentage directly; do not multiply it by Total population to invent an education count.

The High School-or-higher and Bachelor's-or-higher fields are missing for every 2015-2017 row; Below poverty is missing for every 2010-2011 row. Do not fill, interpolate, or treat these missing values as zero.
State coverage includes the 50 states, District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico. Cross-dataset joins may legitimately drop Puerto Rico or District of Columbia when the other table does not cover them.

AVG or MEDIAN across state rows is an unweighted summary of 52 represented state-level geographies, not a population-weighted U.S. national statistic. For education measures, the age-25+ denominator needed for a national weighted rate is not loaded.

White.description: Percentage of population identifying as White alone

Black.description: Percentage of population identifying as Black or African American alone

Asian.description: Percentage of population identifying as Asian alone

Hispanic.description: Percentage of population identifying as Hispanic or Latino (any race)

Education >= High School.description: Percentage of adults age 25+ with at least a high school diploma or GED. The source ACS educational-attainment table defines its universe as the population 25 years and over.

Education >= Bachelor's.description: Percentage of adults age 25+ with at least a bachelor's degree. The source ACS educational-attainment table defines its universe as the population 25 years and over.

Education >= Graduate.description: Percentage of adults age 25+ with a graduate or professional degree. The source ACS educational-attainment table defines its universe as the population 25 years and over.

Income >$50K.description: Percentage of households with annual income above $50,000

Income >$100K.description: Percentage of households with annual income above $100,000

Income >$200K.description: Percentage of households with annual income above $200,000

Median household income.description: Median annual household income in USD

Below poverty.description: Percentage of population living below the federal poverty line

Owner occupied.description: Percentage of housing units that are owner-occupied

Renter occupied.description: Percentage of housing units that are renter-occupied

acs_county.grain: One row per county per year
critical_notes: Runtime coverage is narrower than the upstream ACS source documentation: this table has only Age 18-65, not detailed age bands such as 85+; it has no sex/gender columns and no associate-degree or less-than-9th-grade column.

Race/ethnicity, age, education, income, poverty, and housing fields are separate marginal percentages, not a joint cross-tabulation. They cannot answer intersections such as Hispanic adults with bachelor's degrees or women with graduate degrees.

Education percentages describe adults age 25+, but this table does not contain the number of adults age 25+. Report the percentage directly; do not multiply it by Total population to invent an education count.

The High School-or-higher and Bachelor's-or-higher fields are missing for every 2015-2017 row; Below poverty is missing for every 2010-2011 row and one 2018 county row. Do not fill, interpolate, or treat these missing values as zero.
County coverage varies slightly by year (3,220-3,222 geographies in most years). Count distinct FIPS within the requested year rather than assuming a fixed national county count.

county.description: County name, lowercase, without 'County' suffix. e.g. 'montgomery', 'prince george's'

fips.description: FIPS county code — reliable join key across tables

acs_congress.description: Curated ACS demographic data at the 118th Congressional District level. This runtime table is a subset of the broader upstream ACS documentation and includes only the variables listed below.
acs_congress.grain: One row per congressional district per year
critical_notes: Runtime coverage is narrower than the upstream ACS source documentation: this table has only Age 18-65, not detailed age bands such as 85+; it has no sex/gender columns and no associate-degree or less-than-9th-grade column.

Race/ethnicity, age, education, income, poverty, and housing fields are separate marginal percentages, not a joint cross-tabulation. They cannot answer intersections such as Hispanic adults with bachelor's degrees or women with graduate degrees.

Education percentages describe adults age 25+, but this table does not contain the number of adults age 25+. Report the percentage directly; do not multiply it by Total population to invent an education count.

The High School-or-higher and Bachelor's-or-higher fields are missing for every 2015-2017 row; Below poverty is missing for every 2010-2011 row. Four 2011 district rows are entirely null except for the district/year keys. Do not fill or treat these values as zero.
District identifiers vary across historical years because district configurations changed. Filter to the requested year before counting or joining districts.

cd_118.description: Congressional district code. Format: STATE_ABBR-DD. e.g. 'MD-08'

gov_state.description: Municipal government finance data aggregated at the U.S. state level. Covers balance sheet items, revenue, expenses, debt, pension liability, and derived ratios. Data is for Fiscal Year 2023 only — do not filter by year.
gov_state.source: Reason Foundation GovFinance — standardized government ACFR filings
gov_state.grain: One row per state (single year: FY2023)
gov_state.year_note: Single year only — Fiscal Year 2023. Year column contains string 'Fiscal Year 2023'.
critical_notes: Runtime coverage contains 49 states plus the District of Columbia. Connecticut and Puerto Rico are not present; District of Columbia is a legitimate runtime row.

Rhode Island and Vermont contain zero in every financial field because source filings are unavailable. These rows are missing-data placeholders, not genuine zero-finance governments, and must be excluded from financial rankings and summaries.
The runtime Year label and the current GovFinance source both identify Fiscal Year 2023.

Total_Liabilities.description: Total government liabilities (all obligations) in USD

Current_Assets.description: Short-term assets convertible to cash within one year

Non-Current_Liabilities.description: Long-term obligations due beyond one year. Must be quoted in SQL.

Net_Position.description: Total assets minus total liabilities. Negative = fiscal stress.

Free_Cash_Flow.description: Operating cash flow minus capital expenditures

Bonds,_Loans_&_Notes.description: Outstanding debt from bonds, loans, and notes. MUST be quoted in SQL.

Net_Pension_Liability.description: Unfunded pension obligations owed to government employees. Large values signal long-term fiscal risk.

Net_OPEB_Liability.description: Net Other Post-Employment Benefits liability — unfunded healthcare and other benefits promised to retirees

Compensated_Absences.description: Liability for earned but unused employee leave (vacation, sick days) owed as future cash outflows

POPULATION.description: State population used for per-capita calculations

Current_Ratio.description: Current Assets / Current Liabilities. Value > 1 means government can cover short-term obligations. Value < 1 signals liquidity risk.

Debt_Ratio.description: Total Liabilities / Total Assets. Higher = more leveraged. Value > 1 means liabilities exceed assets.

Year.description: Always 'Fiscal Year 2023'. Do NOT filter by this column — it has only one value.

gov_county.description: Municipal government finance data at the U.S. county level. Same variables as gov_state. Single year: FY2023.
gov_county.source: Reason Foundation GovFinance — standardized government ACFR filings
gov_county.grain: One row per county (single year: FY2023)
critical_notes: Coverage is field-specific rather than complete: the table has 3,057 county geography rows, but only 2,281 have non-null Revenue, 2,247 have non-null Expenses, 2,243 have positive Total Assets, and 2,176 have positive Total Liabilities.

A zero in one financial field does not prove the entire county filing is missing. Exclude NULL for the requested metric and exclude only rows whose core financial fields are all absent/zero; do not apply a blanket Total_Liabilities > 0 filter to unrelated metrics.
Do not treat missing values as zero or include them in lowest-value rankings.

gov_congress.description: Municipal government finance data at the 118th Congressional District level. Same variables as gov_state. Single year: FY2023.
gov_congress.source: Reason Foundation GovFinance — standardized government ACFR filings
gov_congress.grain: One row per congressional district (single year: FY2023)
critical_notes: The table contains 428 district rows rather than a complete 435-seat set because source county-finance coverage does not map to every district.
Twenty district rows contain zero in every financial field and are missing-data placeholders, not genuine zero-finance districts. Exclude them from financial rankings and summaries.
Do not treat missing or placeholder values as zero.

contract_state.description: Processed federal spending and workforce indicators at the U.S. state level. Two rows per state: a 2024 snapshot and a precomputed 2020-2024 summary period. Source: USAspending.gov and payroll aggregates.
contract_state.grain: One row per state per year-period
contract_state.year_type: VARCHAR (not integer — always filter with quoted string e.g. year = '2024')
critical_notes: The '2020-2024' row is a precomputed multi-year summary. Its exact aggregation method is not documented in this repository, so never call it a five-year total or sum it with the 2024 row.
Raw total/count fields match the state spending-breakdown table and are the supported fields in this table.

The source dictionaries define Sub-contract Out, Sub-Contract In, and Net Sub-Contract as concepts requiring state_flow in addition to this table. Because state_flow has no year column, no 2024-only state derivation is supportable from the current runtime files.

Federal Contracts (Indirect) is unavailable in the current runtime. The newest dictionary describes a separate fed_act_obl_indirect source field, while an older dictionary gives a conflicting Contracts plus Net Sub-Contract formula; the physical indirect field is not loaded, so do not derive or report it.

The stored 'Per 1000' fields do NOT reconcile to per-1,000-resident calculations and differ from spending_state by exact agency-count factors. Their denominator/scaling is not traceable; do not use them as per-capita or per-1,000-resident measures. For state-level published per-1,000-resident questions, use spending_state instead.

year.description: Snapshot or summary-period label. Values are '2024' or '2020-2024'. Always quote in SQL. The multi-year row is not proven to be a five-year sum.

Contracts.description: Total federal contract obligations awarded to entities in this state

Contracts Per 1000.description: Stored published normalization labeled 'Per 1000'; it does not reconcile to a resident denominator in this processed table. Do not call it per capita or per 1,000 residents.

Grants.description: Total federal grant awards to entities in this state

Grants Per 1000.description: Stored published normalization with an unverified denominator.

Resident Wage.description: Total federal wages paid to residents of this state

Resident Wage Per 1000.description: Stored published normalization with an unverified denominator.

Direct Payments.description: Federal direct payment transfers (e.g. Social Security, Medicare, benefits)

Direct Payments Per 1000.description: Stored published normalization with an unverified denominator.

Federal Residents.description: Count of federal employees residing in this state

Federal Residents Per 1000.description: Stored published normalization with an unverified denominator.

Employees.description: Federal civilian employees working in this state

Employees Per 1000.description: Stored published normalization with an unverified denominator.

Employees Wage.description: Total wages paid to federal employees working in this state

Employees Wage Per 1000.description: Stored published normalization with an unverified denominator.

finra_state.description: FINRA National Financial Capability Study (NFCS) — financial health indices aggregated at the state level. All metric columns are normalized 0–1 indices (higher = more of that characteristic). Survey data: 2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021 only.
finra_state.grain: One row per state per survey year
critical_notes: Runtime data ends at the 2021 survey wave even though the upstream NFCS site now also offers 2024 data. Do not claim this table contains 2024.
All five measures are normalized indices or shares on a 0-1 scale. They are not percentages unless explicitly multiplied by 100 and labeled as a conversion, and they are not respondent counts.
No respondent count, survey-weight denominator, or population denominator is loaded. Do not multiply a FINRA share or index by ACS population to estimate a resident count.

state.description: Full state name, Title Case. e.g. 'Maryland'. Use LOWER() when joining with other tables.

Year.description: Survey wave year. Only 2009, 2012, 2015, 2018, 2021 exist — do not filter for other years.

financial_constraint.description: Index (0–1) measuring household financial stress: liquidity pressure, difficulty covering expenses, lack of emergency savings. Higher = more constrained/stressed.

alternative_financing.description: Index (0–1) measuring reliance on high-cost non-traditional credit: payday loans, pawn shops, rent-to-own. Higher = more reliance on predatory/alternative finance.

financial_literacy.description: Index (0–1) measuring objective financial knowledge: interest compounding, inflation, bond prices, mortgage math. Higher = more financially literate.

satisfied.description: Share (0–1) of respondents satisfied with their overall financial condition. Higher = more satisfaction.

risk_averse.description: Share (0–1) of respondents with low willingness to take financial risk. Higher = more risk-averse population.

finra_county.description: FINRA NFCS financial health indices at the U.S. county level. 2021 only. Same metrics as finra_state.
critical_notes: This is a partial 2021 county model/estimate file with 2,071 county FIPS geographies, not complete coverage of every U.S. county. National rankings describe only represented counties.
satisfied is null for 9 rows and risk_averse is null for 14 rows. Exclude nulls for those measures rather than treating them as zero.
All measures are normalized indices or shares on a 0-1 scale, not respondent counts.
No respondent count, survey-weight denominator, or population denominator is loaded. Do not multiply a FINRA share or index by ACS population to estimate a resident count.

state.description: Full state name, lowercase. Use LOWER() when joining.

financial_constraint.description: Household financial stress index (0–1). Higher = more stressed.

financial_literacy.description: Objective financial knowledge index (0–1). Higher = more literate.

risk_averse.description: Share unwilling to take financial risk (0–1)

finra_congress.description: FINRA NFCS financial health indices at the 118th Congressional District level. 2021 only.
finra_congress.grain: One row per congressional district (2021 only)
critical_notes: This table contains only the 2021 survey wave; the upstream NFCS site's newer 2024 release is not loaded here.
All measures are normalized indices or shares on a 0-1 scale, not respondent counts.
No respondent count, survey-weight denominator, or population denominator is loaded. Do not multiply a FINRA share or index by an external population to estimate a resident count.

spending_state.description: Federal spending breakdown by state and spending channel. Raw totals match contract_state; this table carries the state-level published per-1,000 values and aligns with the agency detail table. It contains a 2024 snapshot and a precomputed 2020-2024 summary period.
spending_state.grain: One row per state per year-period
critical_notes: Raw total/count fields duplicate contract_state exactly. Never join or add the two tables together; use contract_state for raw state totals and spending_state for state-level published Per 1000 values.
The '2020-2024' row is a precomputed multi-year summary, not a documented five-year sum. Never add it to the 2024 row.

The source dictionary describes these state-level normalized fields as per 1,000 residents and they reconcile to the sum of agency-level normalized values. The exact source population vintage is not included in this repository.

Year.description: Year or period string. Values: '2024' or '2020-2024'. Always quote.

Contracts Per 1000.description: Published contract dollars per 1,000 residents. Exact source population vintage is not loaded.

Grants Per 1000.description: Published grant dollars per 1,000 residents. Exact source population vintage is not loaded.

Resident Wage Per 1000.description: Published resident-wage dollars per 1,000 residents. Exact source population vintage is not loaded.

Direct Payments Per 1000.description: Published direct-payment dollars per 1,000 residents. Exact source population vintage is not loaded.

Federal Residents Per 1000.description: Published federal-resident count per 1,000 residents. Exact source population vintage is not loaded.

Employees Per 1000.description: Published federal-employment count per 1,000 residents. Exact source population vintage is not loaded.

Employees Wage Per 1000.description: Published employee-wage dollars per 1,000 residents. Exact source population vintage is not loaded.

spending_state_agency.description: Federal spending broken down by both state AND federal agency. Allows questions like 'how much did the Department of Defense spend in Maryland'. 21 agency categories × 51 state/DC geographies × 2 year-periods.
spending_state_agency.grain: One row per agency per state per year-period
critical_notes: The table is a complete 21-agency x 51-geography x 2-period grid, but a null metric means no recorded value for that agency/channel. Use COALESCE(metric, 0) only when constructing the documented channel composition; do not call null a reported zero.
The '2020-2024' row is a precomputed multi-year summary, not a documented five-year sum. Never add it to the 2024 row.

For an unspecified agency 'spending' ranking, the documented dashboard composite is Contracts + Grants + Resident Wage. Direct Payments, Employees, Federal Residents, and Employees Wage are separate channels and must not be silently added to that composite.

agency.description: Federal agency name. See agency_values for exact strings to use in WHERE clauses.
sample_values: Department of Health and Human Services

Grants Per 1000.description: Agency grant dollars per 1,000 state residents; sums across agencies to spending_state.

state_flow.description: Federal subaward fund flow records between states and territories. Multiple rows can share the same origin, destination, agency, and NAICS industry, so totals must use SUM(subaward_amount_year). Use for questions about which geographies send or receive the most federal subaward money and through which agencies.
state_flow.grain: Subaward-flow record at prime-state → sub-state, agency, and NAICS dimensions; dimension combinations are not unique
state_flow.geography: state-to-state flow (no year column — annual amounts embedded in subaward_amount_year)
critical_notes: rcpt_st_cd and rcpt_state_name are DUPLICATES — both contain the same full state name in Title Case. Use rcpt_state_name for clarity.
Unnamed: 0 is a row index — never use in queries.
subaward_amount_year can be NEGATIVE (represents adjustments/clawbacks). Use SUM() carefully.
No fiscal year column is available. Treat the file as an all-records snapshot and never attach a year or call it a specific annual total.
Multiple rows share the stated origin/destination/agency/industry dimensions. Always SUM subaward_amount_year after applying filters; never assume one row is the complete flow for a combination.
Totals include intra-state flows unless rcpt_state_name <> subawardee_state_name is explicitly requested. Inflow filters the subawardee side; outflow filters the prime-recipient rcpt side.

rcpt_st_cd.description: Prime awardee state name, Title Case. DUPLICATE of rcpt_state_name — prefer rcpt_state_name.

subawardee_st_cd.description: Sub-awardee state name, Title Case. DUPLICATE of subawardee_state_name — prefer subawardee_state_name.

rcpt_state_name.description: Full name of the prime awardee state (receives federal award and issues subawards). Title Case.

subawardee_state_name.description: Full name of the sub-awardee state (receives money downstream from prime). Title Case.

subaward_amount_year.description: Dollar amount of the subaward flow. Can be negative (adjustments). SUM() across rows for totals.

county_flow.description: Federal subaward fund flow data between U.S. counties. Each row is a prime-awardee county to sub-awardee county money flow with coordinates for mapping. Covers fiscal years 2010–2024.
county_flow.grain: One row per prime-county → sub-county flow per agency per fiscal year
critical_notes: Geographic coverage is incomplete: origin and destination rows cover 45 state/territory names and omit Alabama, Alaska, Arizona, Arkansas, California, Colorado, and Connecticut. National rankings are rankings within the represented flow records, not all U.S. counties.
subaward_amount can be negative because of adjustments/clawbacks. SUM returns a net amount.
Totals include intra-county flows unless rcpt_cty <> subawardee_cty is explicitly requested. Inflow filters the subawardee side; outflow filters the prime-recipient rcpt side.
County names repeat across states; use FIPS or the *_full_name fields instead of filtering on county name alone.

rcpt_cty.description: FIPS code of the prime awardee county (receives federal award)

subawardee_cty.description: FIPS code of the sub-awardee county (receives money downstream)

rcpt_cty_name.description: Full name of prime awardee county including state. e.g. 'Montgomery County'

rcpt_state.description: State of prime awardee, Title Case

rcpt_full_name.description: Full identifier of prime awardee: 'County Name, State Name'

subawardee_full_name.description: Full identifier of sub-awardee: 'County Name, State Name'

act_dt_fis_yr.description: Federal fiscal year of the award

agency_name.description: Federal agency that issued the prime award
sample_values: Department of Health and Human Services

origin_lat.description: Latitude of prime awardee county centroid

origin_lon.description: Longitude of prime awardee county centroid

congress_flow.description: Federal subaward fund flow records between 118th Congressional Districts for fiscal years 2020-2024. Multiple rows may share the same origin, destination, agency, year, and NAICS code, so totals must use SUM(subaward_amount). Integer district identifiers use numeric STCD118 encoding and must be canonicalized before joining to cd_118 strings.
congress_flow.grain: Subaward-flow record at prime-district → sub-district, agency, fiscal-year, and NAICS dimensions; dimension combinations are not unique
critical_notes: prime_awardee_stcd118 and subawardee_stcd118 are INTEGER codes (e.g. 200, 101), not the standard 'AK-00' / 'MD-08' string. Do not compare them directly. contract_congress supplies state_fips; ACS/FINRA/government congress tables must first bridge cd_118 through a DISTINCT contract_congress cd_118/state_fips mapping before canonicalization.
Use rcpt_cd_name for human-readable district names like 'Alaska CD-00', 'Maryland CD-08'.
Unnamed: 0 is a row index — never use in queries.
naics_2digit_code is FLOAT here (not integer) due to nulls.
Multiple rows share the stated origin/destination/agency/year/industry dimensions. Always SUM subaward_amount after applying filters.
subaward_amount can be negative because of adjustments/clawbacks. SUM returns a net amount.

Totals include intra-district flows unless the origin and destination district codes are explicitly constrained to differ. Inflow filters the subawardee side; outflow filters the prime-recipient rcpt side.

contract_state_agency.description: Federal spending broken down by BOTH agency AND state. Allows questions like 'how much did the Department of Defense spend in Maryland' or 'which agency gives the most grants to Texas'. 21 agencies × 50 states × 2 year-periods = 2,142 rows. Also includes employee and wage breakdown.
contract_state_agency.grain: One row per agency per state per year-period

cross_table_joins.warning: State names have THREE different casings. Always normalize with LOWER() when joining. FIPS codes are the safest join key for county-level joins.

patterns.acs_to_finra_state: JOIN on LOWER(acs_state.state) = LOWER(finra_state.state). Filter each source to its requested/default period separately; do not equate year fields when periods differ.
patterns.acs_to_contract_state: JOIN on LOWER(acs_state.state) = LOWER(contract_state.state) — note contract year is VARCHAR
patterns.county_join_preferred: Use fips as join key for county tables: acs_county.fips = gov_county.fips = finra_county.fips
patterns.congress_join: JOIN on cd_118 directly across ACS/FINRA/government/contract congress tables. For congress_flow, contract_congress supplies the cd_118/state_fips mapping: join ACS/FINRA/government cd_118 to a DISTINCT contract_congress mapping, then canonicalize state_fips plus the district number into numeric STCD118.
patterns.agency_filter: Use LIKE for agency: WHERE agency LIKE '%Defense%' or exact string 'Department of Defense'

cross_table_joins.example_multi_table_query: SELECT a.state, a.financial_literacy, g.Net_Pension_Liability_per_capita FROM finra_state a JOIN gov_state g ON LOWER(a.state) = LOWER(g.state) WHERE a.Year = 2021 ORDER BY a.financial_literacy DESC
cross_table_joins.agency_tables: spending_state_agency has an 'agency' column — always filter with an exact string such as WHERE agency = 'Department of Defense'
cross_table_joins.flow_to_other_tables: state_flow uses normalized state-name joins. county_flow uses integer FIPS: rcpt_cty/subawardee_cty joins to contract_county.county_fips or other county tables' fips. congress_flow uses numeric STCD118 codes. contract_congress has state_fips; for ACS/FINRA/government congress tables, first bridge cd_118 through DISTINCT contract_congress cd_118/state_fips, then canonicalize state_fips + district number.
cross_table_joins.congress_flow_warning: congress_flow district ids are INTEGER (e.g. 200), not 'MD-08'. Never join them directly to cd_118 strings; use the documented canonical conversion.

common_question_patterns.highest_lowest: Use ORDER BY col DESC/ASC LIMIT N
common_question_patterns.gov_tables_no_year_filter: gov_state/county/congress have only one year — never add a year filter
common_question_patterns.per_capita_comparison: Use _per_capita columns for fair cross-state/county comparison
common_question_patterns.finra_interpretation: Higher financial_literacy = more literate population. Higher financial_constraint = more stressed.
common_question_patterns.flow_total: For state_flow use SUM(subaward_amount_year); for county_flow/congress_flow use SUM(subaward_amount). Group the rcpt_* side for originating/outflow totals and the subawardee_* side for destination/inflow totals.
